To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the Paleozoic KKG and Cenozoic granites in vicinity of the South Tibetan detachment zone in Himachal High-Himalaya are intensely deformed; (2) deformation of the granites is synchronous with the ductile deformation along STD zone; (3) the KKG preserves its fabric in the interior part, whereas the Cenozoics leucogranitic bodies are tectonically modified in the vicinity of STD zone; and (4)

the KKG and Cenozoic granites were intruded into the High Himalaya in Paleozoic and Cenozoics respectively and their fabric were modified by the post-emplacement ductility deformation along the STD.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the KKG and leucogranitic intrusions in the vicinity of the STD were subjected to ductile deformation and the fabric of the granites was modified by the Cretaceous–Cenozoic tectonics along the STD.
the KKG and leucogranitic intrusions are not only deformed in vicinity to the STD zone but are also modified by post-intrusion deformation.
